prompt: Hypothetical. A paper fill is Rs 806 for 12 shares. A real fill would have been Rs 808 for the same 12 shares. What is the rupee effect of the worse fill?
A paper trade shows a profit of Rs 1,200. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A paper profit is the same as a live profit.
It is a hypothetical result. Real fills, costs and your own behaviour could make a live result different.
It is a live result, because the script recorded it.
It proves the rule works with real money.

explanations.a: A paper profit assumes fills that may not happen in real trading. It is not the same as a live profit.
explanations.c: The script records hypothetical trades. Recording a trade does not make it live.
explanations.d: A paper result does not show how the rule works with real money. Real money adds delays, costs and emotion.

prompt: The script finds a missing price for one symbol on a trading day. What should it do?

options.text: Skip that symbol and carry on with the rest.
Stop, report the bad data, and record no fill for that symbol.
Use yesterday's price and record it as today's.
Fill the trade at zero rupees.

explanations.a: Skipping hides the gap. The result then looks complete when it is not.
explanations.c: Using an old price and labelling it as new is a guess. The record would be false.
explanations.d: A zero fill is not a real price. It would give a false result.

prompt: Which is the role of the Kite demo in this book?

options.text: It is a forward test.
It is for practice with the screens, using dummy data. It is not a forward test.
It is a live account with small money.
It is a backtest of past prices.

explanations.a: The demo uses dummy data for interface practice. It does not follow fixed rules through live prices.
explanations.c: The book never asks you to place a real order. The demo is not a live account.
explanations.d: A backtest uses past data and rules applied after the fact. The demo is for practice with the screens.

prompt: Hypothetical. The script's data is missing on a market holiday, but the script records a fill for that day. What is the main error?

options.text: The script should record fills on holidays, because prices exist.
The holiday list was not checked, so the script recorded a fill when the market was closed. It should stop and use the verified holiday list.
The fill should be recorded as live.
Nothing is wrong, because a missing price is harmless.

explanations.a: A market holiday has no trading session. A fill on that day is a false record.
explanations.c: Changing the mode to live makes the error worse. No real orders were sent.
explanations.d: A missing price is a warning sign. The script must stop rather than record a fill.

prompt: A forward log has this row: 'Week 1. Mode: live. Trades recorded on paper. No orders sent.' Which part is wrong?

options.text: 'Week 1', because the log should not have a week label
'Mode: live', because a paper test must be labelled forward, not live
'No orders sent', because it should say orders were sent
'Trades recorded on paper', because paper trades cannot be recorded

explanations.a: A week label is useful and is not the error.
explanations.c: No orders should be sent in a forward test. That part of the row is correct.
explanations.d: Paper trades are recorded as hypothetical fills. That part of the row is correct.
